ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (28) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

«Добро» (dobro, 'good') and «доброта» (dobrota, 'kindness') are kept distinct, as is «злость» (zlost', 'malice'). In the Confucius saying the Russian prints «равны» (ravny, 'are equal') where the familiar saying (Analects 6.20) has 'are not equal'; it is translated as printed and flagged. Luke 6:46–49 is translated from Tolstoy's Russian, with «господи» (gospodi) as 'Lord'.

Source observation: [6] The Confucius saying reads «Те, кто знают истину, равны тем, которые любят ее» ('those who know the truth are equal to those who love it'); the parallel clause and the source saying (Analects 6.20) suggest a dropped «не» ('not'): «не равны». Translated as printed.
